items.setupText: Choose the grammatically correct completion.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Reads remoteness without confusing it with past time or obligation.
audit.levelReason: Requires discriminating scenario framing from asserted events.
audit.similarityNote: An interview-style contingency question imagines network failure.

items.setupText: Choose the connector that leaves approval unsettled and makes it a condition for release.
items.taskText: Approval is still pending. The dataset can be released ___ the review panel authorizes it.
items.explanation: Provided that leaves authorization open and makes release conditional on it.

rationales.given that: Given that treats authorization as an accepted premise, contrary to its pending status.
rationales.provided that: Provided that leaves authorization open and makes release conditional on it.
rationales.now that: Now that presents authorization as a newly established fact.
rationales.seeing that: Seeing that supplies an accepted reason rather than an unresolved condition.

findings: Final-vote policy item wrongly ruled out receive in an otherwise valid open conditional.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Maintains factual uncertainty in formal administrative writing.
audit.levelReason: Requires a precise distinction among plausible formal connectors.
audit.similarityNote: Pending authorization contrasts with fact-presupposing reason clauses.

items.setupText: Choose the formal rewrite with the same past counterfactual meaning.
items.taskText: 'Without the emergency grant, the theatre would have closed last winter.'
options: Were it not for the emergency grant, the theatre would close next winter.
Had it not been for the emergency grant, the theatre would have closed last winter.
Should the emergency grant arrive, the theatre will remain open.
Had the theatre closed, the emergency grant would have arrived.
items.answer: Had it not been for the emergency grant, the theatre would have closed last winter.
items.explanation: Had it not been for expands without into a formal inverted condition about missing past support.

rationales.Were it not for the emergency grant, the: This shifts the condition and closure to a present/future hypothesis.
rationales.Should the emergency grant arrive, the t: This treats the grant as a future possibility rather than support that prevented a past closure.
rationales.Had the theatre closed, the emergency gr: This reverses the dependency, making closure a condition for the grant.
rationales.Had it not been for the emergency grant,: Had it not been for expands without into a formal inverted condition about missing past support.

findings: Appendix-note objection item repeated the same routine modal selection.
audit.microSkill: Had it not been for as past enabling-condition inversion
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves both polarity and past reference in a formal paraphrase.
audit.levelReason: A compact without-phrase must be expanded into a complex conditional.
audit.similarityNote: An emergency grant prevented a past theatre closure.

items.setupText: Choose the completion that acknowledges a possible loss without asserting that it has occurred.
items.taskText: The result is not yet known. ___ we lose the contract, we will continue the research.
items.explanation: Even if treats losing as an unconfirmed possibility that will not change the research plan.

rationales.Even if: Even if treats losing as an unconfirmed possibility that will not change the research plan.
rationales.Even though: Even though normally treats the loss as a conceded fact, which the prompt does not establish.
rationales.Now that: Now that presents the loss as an established new circumstance.
rationales.Given that: Given that adopts the loss as an accepted premise rather than leaving it unsettled.

findings: Agenda/advisory brief item had an unnatural tail and a basic would-make target.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves uncertainty when conceding an adverse scenario.
audit.levelReason: The distinction depends on factual commitment rather than basic grammar.
audit.similarityNote: An undecided contract result does not alter research plans.

items.setupText: Choose the function of the if-clause.
items.taskText: 'If I remember correctly, the lease expires in November.'
options: It qualifies the reliability of the speaker's claim.
It postpones giving the date until the speaker has checked the lease.
It asks the listener to confirm the date before the speaker gives it.
It signals that the lease contains two possible expiry dates.
items.answer: It qualifies the reliability of the speaker's claim.
items.explanation: The clause signals that the assertion depends on the accuracy of the speaker's memory.

rationales.It postpones giving the date until the s: The speaker gives November immediately, while qualifying confidence in that information.
rationales.It asks the listener to confirm the date: The phrase limits the speaker's confidence; it does not explicitly request prior confirmation.
rationales.It qualifies the reliability of the spea: The clause signals that the assertion depends on the accuracy of the speaker's memory.
rationales.It signals that the lease contains two p: The uncertainty belongs to the speaker's memory, not to the lease's contractual provisions.

findings: Examination-committee item repeated would approve and added no interpretive challenge.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes a condition on confidence rather than on the event itself.
audit.levelReason: Pragmatic scope distinguishes an assertion hedge from an event condition.
audit.similarityNote: Memory accuracy qualifies an expiry-date claim.

items.setupText: Choose the explanation of 'will' in the if-clause.
items.taskText: 'I'll redraw the chart if it will make the results easier to compare.'
options: The redraw depends on the listener's willingness to compare the results.
The speaker promises to redraw it before assessing whether that will help.
The comparison has already become easier.
The anticipated benefit is the condition for deciding to redraw it.
items.answer: The anticipated benefit is the condition for deciding to redraw it.
items.explanation: The speaker bases the decision to act on the expected usefulness of that action.

rationales.The redraw depends on the listener's wil: The clause concerns the redraw's expected effect, not another person's willingness to cooperate.
rationales.The anticipated benefit is the condition: The speaker bases the decision to act on the expected usefulness of that action.
rationales.The speaker promises to redraw it before: The expected benefit determines whether to redraw; the promise is conditional rather than unconditional.
rationales.The comparison has already become easier: 'Will make' points to a prospective effect, not a completed improvement.

findings: Evidence-table finding item was a repeated would-be exercise with an awkward tail.
audit.microSkill: Will for a later benefit within an if-clause
audit.pedagogicalValue: Explains a valid use of will after if when an action depends on its expected result.
audit.levelReason: Requires distinguishing the decision condition from chronological event order.
audit.similarityNote: Expected benefit justifies a proposed chart revision.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves uncertainty about what happened yesterday.
items.taskText: The engineer has not yet established whether the valve was closed. She wants to state a consequence conditional on it having been closed.
options: If the valve was closed, the leak should have stopped.
If the valve had been closed, the leak would have stopped, but it wasn't.
Since the valve was closed, the leak must have stopped.
The valve was closed, so the leak stopped.
items.answer: If the valve was closed, the leak should have stopped.
items.explanation: The open past if-clause leaves closure undecided; should have states its expected consequence.

rationales.If the valve had been closed, the leak w: But it wasn't explicitly denies closure and removes the required uncertainty.
rationales.Since the valve was closed, the leak mus: Since accepts closure as fact rather than leaving it to be established.
rationales.The valve was closed, so the leak stoppe: This asserts both closure and stopping as actual events.
rationales.If the valve was closed, the leak should: The open past if-clause leaves closure undecided; should have states its expected consequence.

findings: Policy-draft training item both rejected receive and ended with an incomplete time reference.
audit.microSkill: Open past reasoning versus known-false counterfactual
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps an investigation's unknown premise separate from its expected consequence.
audit.levelReason: The learner must preserve epistemic status across complete alternatives.
audit.similarityNote: An engineering investigation leaves a past valve position unknown.

items.setupText: Choose the completion that describes the ongoing consequence now of an unreal past action.
items.taskText: We ignored the early complaints, so the dispute is still consuming our time. If we'd responded then, we ___ with it now.
items.explanation: Wouldn't be dealing gives an imagined ongoing present result of responding differently in the past.

rationales.wouldn't be dealing: Wouldn't be dealing gives an imagined ongoing present result of responding differently in the past.
rationales.wouldn't have dealt: The perfect simple presents a completed past response rather than an activity continuing now.
rationales.hadn't dealt: Hadn't dealt describes an earlier past situation, not a modal consequence now.
rationales.haven't dealt: Haven't dealt asserts actual non-action, conflicting with the ongoing dispute and hypothetical result.

findings: Assessment-rubric objection item ended a repetitive set of basic second-conditionals.
audit.microSkill: Mixed conditional with a progressive present result
audit.pedagogicalValue: Combines a past missed response with its continuing current consequence.
audit.levelReason: Requires coordinating counterfactual time, negation and progressive aspect.
audit.similarityNote: Ignored complaints create an ongoing burden now.

items.setupText: Choose what the conditional itself establishes about whether the memo was read.
items.taskText: 'If the auditors had read the memo, they would have raised precisely the objection we see in their report. We still need to check whether they received it.'
options: It establishes that the auditors did not read the memo.
It establishes that the auditors received but ignored the memo.
It establishes that reading the memo was the only possible source of the objection.
It leaves reading unresolved while assessing its expected consequence.
items.answer: It leaves reading unresolved while assessing its expected consequence.
items.explanation: The speaker considers what reading would lead to without resolving whether reading occurred.

rationales.It establishes that the auditors did not: A past-perfect conditional often suggests a contrary-to-fact premise, but this context explicitly leaves reading unresolved.
rationales.It establishes that the auditors receive: Receipt and neglect are not established; the next sentence calls for checking receipt.
rationales.It leaves reading unresolved while asses: The speaker considers what reading would lead to without resolving whether reading occurred.
rationales.It establishes that reading the memo was: An expected consequence does not establish that its proposed cause was the only possible cause.

findings: Original C2 item required only a participle after had and reused generic feedback.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids treating a common implication of a conditional form as an unavoidable factual assertion.
audit.levelReason: Requires integrating discourse evidence with a defeasible grammatical inference.
audit.similarityNote: An observed objection is compatible with an unresolved past premise.

items.setupText: Choose the paraphrase that preserves the exception and its negation exactly.
items.taskText: 'The permit remains valid unless the holder fails to renew the insurance.'
options: If the holder fails to renew the insurance, the permit remains valid.
If the holder does not fail to renew the insurance, the permit remains valid.
The permit remains valid only if the holder fails to renew the insurance.
Unless the holder renews the insurance, the permit remains valid.
items.answer: If the holder does not fail to renew the insurance, the permit remains valid.
items.explanation: Unless negates the whole exception, including fails: in the absence of failure to renew, validity continues.

rationales.If the holder fails to renew the insuran: This turns the stated exception into a condition guaranteeing continued validity.
rationales.If the holder does not fail to renew the: Unless negates the whole exception, including fails: in the absence of failure to renew, validity continues.
rationales.The permit remains valid only if the hol: Only if makes failure necessary for validity, reversing the original protection.
rationales.Unless the holder renews the insurance,: This makes renewal, rather than failure to renew, the exception.

findings: Schedule item repeated the same had-plus-participle exercise at C2.
audit.microSkill: Negation scope inside an unless exception
audit.pedagogicalValue: Tracks a negative lexical predicate when expanding unless.
audit.levelReason: The embedded failure condition requires precise scope handling.
audit.similarityNote: Unless applies to the entire failure-to-renew proposition.

items.setupText: Choose the rule that makes approval both necessary and sufficient for release.
items.taskText: The editor wants to state two commitments: without approval there is no release, and approval guarantees release.
options: The report will be released if approval is granted.
The report will be released if and only if approval is granted.
The report will be released only if approval is granted.
The report may be released if approval is granted.
items.answer: The report will be released if and only if approval is granted.
items.explanation: If and only if states both directions: approval is required and is enough for release.

rationales.The report will be released if approval: If grants the approval-to-release direction but does not rule out release by another route.
rationales.The report will be released only if appr: Only if makes approval necessary but does not promise release when approval is granted.
rationales.The report may be released if approval i: May gives a possibility even after approval, not the requested guarantee.
rationales.The report will be released if and only: If and only if states both directions: approval is required and is enough for release.

findings: Summary item offered routine written/have written/to write/writing choices without C2 interpretation.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Writes an exact rule when both necessity and sufficiency are intended.
audit.levelReason: Requires comparing the logical commitments of closely related grammatical sentences.
audit.similarityNote: Two explicitly requested directions require if and only if.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation supported by the reply.
items.taskText: 'Would you endorse the plan?' 'Not if it involves compulsory overtime.'
options: Removing compulsory overtime guarantees the speaker's endorsement.
The speaker asserts that the plan already involves compulsory overtime.
Compulsory overtime would rule out the speaker's endorsement.
The speaker endorses compulsory overtime but questions the rest of the plan.
items.answer: Compulsory overtime would rule out the speaker's endorsement.
items.explanation: Not if supplies a condition under which the answer to endorsing is no.

rationales.Compulsory overtime would rule out the s: Not if supplies a condition under which the answer to endorsing is no.
rationales.Removing compulsory overtime guarantees: Ruling out one condition for refusal does not guarantee endorsement for other reasons.
rationales.The speaker asserts that the plan alread: The reply identifies a possible disqualifier without asserting that it is present.
rationales.The speaker endorses compulsory overtime: The specified objection is to compulsory overtime; no endorsement of it is expressed.

findings: Email item tested only sent after inverted had and gave identical-style error messages.
audit.microSkill: Conditional negation in an elliptical reply
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recovers the omitted negative result without strengthening its converse.
audit.levelReason: Requires discourse reconstruction and careful limits on inference.
audit.similarityNote: A short not-if reply supplies a sufficient reason to refuse.

items.setupText: Choose the function of 'if anything' in this response.
items.taskText: 'The revisions have made the policy harsher.' 'If anything, they've made it more flexible.'
options: The speaker remains neutral between the two assessments.
The speaker cautiously proposes the opposite assessment.
Flexibility depends on whether any revision exists.
The speaker agrees that harshness and flexibility increased equally.
items.answer: The speaker cautiously proposes the opposite assessment.
items.explanation: 'If anything' introduces a tentative correction in the opposite direction: more flexible rather than harsher.

rationales.The speaker remains neutral between the: The hedge is cautious, but the speaker does favor the opposite assessment, more flexible.
rationales.Flexibility depends on whether any revis: This is an idiomatic corrective phrase, not an ordinary event condition.
rationales.The speaker cautiously proposes the oppo: 'If anything' introduces a tentative correction in the opposite direction: more flexible rather than harsher.
rationales.The speaker agrees that harshness and fl: The reply challenges the first assessment; it does not endorse both equally.

findings: List item repeated participle selection and supplied no advanced semantic contrast.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes when an if-expression operates on an assessment rather than linking events.
audit.levelReason: Pragmatic interpretation depends on the preceding claim and corrective force.
audit.similarityNote: An idiomatic if-phrase tentatively reverses another speaker's evaluation.

items.setupText: Choose the edit that unambiguously expresses the intended modest claim.
items.taskText: The writer means 'The study is useful, but I am not claiming it is indispensable.' The draft says, 'The study is useful, if not indispensable.'
options: The study is useful, though not necessarily indispensable.
The study is indispensable, if not useful.
If the study is indispensable, it is useful.
The study is useful only if it is indispensable.
items.answer: The study is useful, though not necessarily indispensable.
items.explanation: Though not necessarily explicitly withholds the stronger claim and avoids the draft's possible 'perhaps even' reading.

rationales.The study is indispensable, if not usefu: This promotes indispensable to the asserted description, stronger than intended.
rationales.The study is useful, though not necessar: Though not necessarily explicitly withholds the stronger claim and avoids the draft's possible 'perhaps even' reading.
rationales.If the study is indispensable, it is use: This makes usefulness conditional on indispensability rather than asserting usefulness directly.
rationales.The study is useful only if it is indisp: Only if makes indispensability necessary for usefulness, which the intended modest claim does not require.

findings: Lesson item repeated had-plus-participle and relied on superficial vocabulary change.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Replaces a potentially ambiguous scalar phrase when precise commitment matters.
audit.levelReason: Requires sensitivity to competing concessive and intensifying readings.
audit.similarityNote: An editing task resolves the two possible readings of if not.

items.setupText: Choose the sentence that expresses regret about the past, without making a rule about evidence.
items.taskText: The curator trusted an unreliable account and now wishes she had checked it.
options: Only if I had checked the account would I have trusted it.
If I check the account, I can decide whether to trust it.
If only I had checked the account before trusting it.
If only I check the account, the decision is mine.
items.answer: If only I had checked the account before trusting it.
items.explanation: If only plus past perfect expresses a wish that a completed past choice had been different.

rationales.Only if I had checked the account would: Only if states a necessary condition for trusting; it does not express the curator's regret.
rationales.If I check the account, I can decide whe: This sets up a current or future checking condition rather than wishing the past were different.
rationales.If only I check the account, the decisio: Here only restricts the subject I; it does not form the intended past regret.
rationales.If only I had checked the account before: If only plus past perfect expresses a wish that a completed past choice had been different.

findings: Printing item tested an obvious participle and asserted a questionable printer-jam consequence.
audit.microSkill: If only versus only if and subject-focus only
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes regret from restrictive conditional meanings through word order.
audit.levelReason: Closely related strings carry different scope and communicative functions.
audit.similarityNote: Three placements of only compete with a past wish.

items.setupText: Choose the statement licensed by the rule without deciding whether the exception occurs.
items.taskText: 'The files will be opened to researchers unless both the donor objects and the committee upholds the objection.'
options: If either the donor objects or the committee objects, the files must stay closed.
The donor's objection alone prevents the files from being opened.
The committee has already upheld the donor's objection.
If the donor objects but the committee rejects the objection, the files will be opened.
items.answer: If the donor objects but the committee rejects the objection, the files will be opened.
items.explanation: The exception requires both stated events; rejection by the committee means that combined exception is absent.

rationales.If the donor objects but the committee r: The exception requires both stated events; rejection by the committee means that combined exception is absent.
rationales.If either the donor objects or the commi: This substitutes either/or for the rule's both/and and changes the committee's action.
rationales.The donor's objection alone prevents the: The donor's objection alone does not meet the two-part exception.
rationales.The committee has already upheld the don: The rule sets a future condition; it reports no completed committee decision.

findings: Office-opening item was a repeated elementary participle completion with C2 labelling.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves both parts of a compound exception when drawing a consequence.
audit.levelReason: Requires tracking negation over a two-part condition in natural language.
audit.similarityNote: A donor objection matters only in conjunction with committee support.

items.setupText: Choose the distinction accurately made by the two versions.
items.taskText: A: 'Even if the witness is mistaken, the timestamps establish the sequence.' B: 'Even though the witness is mistaken, the timestamps establish the sequence.'
options: A leaves the mistake open; B presents it as a conceded fact.
A asserts the mistake more firmly than B does.
B makes the timestamps depend on the witness being correct.
A and B both deny that the timestamps establish the sequence.
items.answer: A leaves the mistake open; B presents it as a conceded fact.
items.explanation: The difference is factual commitment to the concession, while the claim about the timestamps remains.

rationales.A asserts the mistake more firmly than B: Even if does not itself assert the mistake; even though normally concedes it as fact.
rationales.B makes the timestamps depend on the wit: B says the timestamps establish the sequence despite the mistake, not because the witness is correct.
rationales.A leaves the mistake open; B presents it: The difference is factual commitment to the concession, while the claim about the timestamps remains.
rationales.A and B both deny that the timestamps es: Both versions assert the evidential role of the timestamps.

findings: Questions item repeated answered after had and omitted any advanced interpretation.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Edits evidential stance without changing the main claim.
audit.levelReason: Requires comparing the precise commitments of minimally differing whole sentences.
audit.similarityNote: Two versions differ only in whether a witness's mistake is conceded.

items.setupText: Choose the equivalent condition for withholding access.
items.taskText: 'If either the identity check or the payment check is incomplete, access must be withheld.'
options: Access must be withheld only when both checks are incomplete.
If the two checks are not both complete, access must be withheld.
If either check is complete, access must be withheld.
If neither check is incomplete, access must be withheld.
items.answer: If the two checks are not both complete, access must be withheld.
items.explanation: Not both complete covers either incomplete check or both incomplete checks, preserving the original trigger.

rationales.Access must be withheld only when both c: The original triggers withholding when even one check is incomplete, not only when both are.
rationales.If the two checks are not both complete,: Not both complete covers either incomplete check or both incomplete checks, preserving the original trigger.
rationales.If either check is complete, access must: A complete check is not itself the reason for withholding; the other check's status matters.
rationales.If neither check is incomplete, access m: Neither incomplete means both complete, reversing the triggering condition.

findings: Notice item reduced C2 to selecting read and posited an unexplained tutor consequence.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves a compound access rule when changing its logical form.
audit.levelReason: Careful scope control distinguishes not both from neither.
audit.similarityNote: Two independent checks define an access restriction.

items.setupText: Choose the rewrite that makes only the appendix, not the main report, depend on consent.
items.taskText: The main report will be published regardless. The appendix will be included only with the interviewees' consent.
options: If the interviewees consent, we will publish both the report and the appendix; otherwise neither will appear.
We will publish the report only if the interviewees consent, and we may include the appendix.
If we publish the report, the interviewees will consent to the appendix.
We will publish the report; we will include the appendix only if the interviewees consent.
items.answer: We will publish the report; we will include the appendix only if the interviewees consent.
items.explanation: Separate clauses keep the report unconditional and attach the consent requirement specifically to the appendix.

rationales.If the interviewees consent, we will pub: This makes the main report conditional too, contrary to its unconditional publication.
rationales.We will publish the report only if the i: This attaches consent to the report and leaves the appendix without the intended restriction.
rationales.If we publish the report, the interviewe: This reverses the dependency and predicts consent from publication.
rationales.We will publish the report; we will incl: Separate clauses keep the report unconditional and attach the consent requirement specifically to the appendix.

findings: Topic-choice original was another participle exercise without a C2 decision.
audit.microSkill: Scope of a condition over coordinated actions
audit.pedagogicalValue: Prevents a condition from accidentally governing the wrong publication action.
audit.levelReason: Requires precise editing of scope across multiple commitments.
audit.similarityNote: Consent restricts an appendix while the main publication remains unconditional.

items.setupText: Choose the formal sentence preserving a present absence and a current hypothetical result.
items.taskText: There is no independent audit. With one, we could place greater confidence in the figures now.
options: Were there an independent audit, we could place greater confidence in the figures now.
Had there been an independent audit last year, we could have trusted last year's figures.
Should an independent audit arrive next year, we will trust the figures then.
Since there is an independent audit, we can place greater confidence in the figures now.
items.answer: Were there an independent audit, we could place greater confidence in the figures now.
items.explanation: Were there imagines reversing the present absence; could preserves a current hypothetical possibility.

rationales.Were there an independent audit, we coul: Were there imagines reversing the present absence; could preserves a current hypothetical possibility.
rationales.Had there been an independent audit last: This moves both the condition and the trust judgment to last year.
rationales.Should an independent audit arrive next: This changes the present alternative into a future contingency and future judgment.
rationales.Since there is an independent audit, we: Since asserts the audit's existence, contrary to the stated absence.

findings: Plan item repeated a made participle choice rather than testing formal conditional meaning.
audit.microSkill: Existential inversion with controlled time and factual status
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves a present hypothetical assessment in a formal rewrite.
audit.levelReason: Requires concurrent control of inversion, modality and factual commitment.
audit.similarityNote: Existential were there expresses the absence of independent verification.

items.setupText: Choose the completion that links an ongoing unreal past activity with the situation now.
items.taskText: The overnight log shows no monitoring took place, and we are still reconstructing the failure. If someone ___ the system during the outage, we would now know where it began.
items.explanation: Had been monitoring imagines sustained observation during the past outage; its information would be available now.

rationales.is monitoring: Is monitoring describes activity now, not an unreal activity during the completed outage.
rationales.will have monitored: Will have monitored places completion in the future and cannot supply the missing observation from the outage.
rationales.had been monitoring: Had been monitoring imagines sustained observation during the past outage; its information would be available now.
rationales.were to start monitoring: This imagines a prospective start rather than sustained observation during the completed outage.

findings: File item required only found after had and gave no meaningful advanced contrast.
audit.microSkill: Past-perfect progressive condition with present knowledge result
audit.pedagogicalValue: Relates missing sustained observation to a current information gap.
audit.levelReason: Integrates aspect, counterfactual time and a present epistemic consequence.
audit.similarityNote: An unreal monitoring process would have supplied knowledge now.

items.setupText: Choose the meaning of 'if only to' in this recommendation.
items.taskText: 'You should attend the briefing, if only to learn who is responsible for the handover.'
options: Attendance is advisable only if finding out who is responsible is your purpose.
Finding out who is responsible is the one benefit the speaker allows that attendance could offer.
Finding out who is responsible is reason enough to attend, whatever other benefits there may be.
Whether attendance is advisable remains uncertain until you know who is responsible.
items.answer: Finding out who is responsible is reason enough to attend, whatever other benefits there may be.
items.explanation: 'If only to' presents a modest benefit as sufficient reason to attend without excluding additional benefits.

rationales.Attendance is advisable only if finding: This turns the highlighted reason into a necessary condition on your purpose; 'if only to' offers it as sufficient support for attending.
rationales.Finding out who is responsible is reason: 'If only to' presents a modest benefit as sufficient reason to attend without excluding additional benefits.
rationales.Finding out who is responsible is the on: 'Only' highlights a minimum justification here; it does not restrict the briefing to a single possible benefit.
rationales.Whether attendance is advisable remains: The recommendation is already made. The phrase supplies a reason to attend, not an unresolved condition delaying the advice.

findings: Original class item tested taught after had and supplied an unsupported replacement consequence.
The first replacement used irrelevant prohibition and weak regret distractors; replaced with competing scope readings after coordinator review.
audit.microSkill: Minimal justification versus necessary purpose, exclusive benefit and uncertainty
audit.pedagogicalValue: Reads if only to as a sufficient minimal reason without importing only-if restrictions.
audit.levelReason: All alternatives are natural interpretations requiring precise control of argumentative scope.
audit.similarityNote: A briefing recommendation contrasts four plausible readings of the same idiom.

items.setupText: Choose the speaker's rhetorical purpose.
items.taskText: After residents were given two minutes to respond, a councillor says, 'If that counts as consultation, the word has lost its meaning.'
options: To announce a neutral definition of consultation.
To confirm that residents approved the proposal.
To challenge whether the process deserves the label consultation.
To suggest the process merely needs a different name.
items.answer: To challenge whether the process deserves the label consultation.
items.explanation: The conditional tests a disputed classification and uses an unacceptable consequence to challenge it.

rationales.To announce a neutral definition of cons: The context and exaggerated consequence express criticism, not a neutral definition.
rationales.To confirm that residents approved the p: Nothing in the remark reports approval by residents.
rationales.To suggest the process merely needs a di: The councillor criticizes the process's failure to involve residents; changing its name alone does not address that criticism.
rationales.To challenge whether the process deserve: The conditional tests a disputed classification and uses an unacceptable consequence to challenge it.

findings: Documents item offered basic brought selection and an arbitrary link to finding an entrance.
audit.pedagogicalValue: Recognizes criticism carried by a conditional rather than reading it as a literal prediction.
audit.levelReason: Requires interpreting argumentative force from discourse and a figurative consequence.
audit.similarityNote: A councillor challenges the label assigned to a public process.

items.setupText: Choose the inference justified by the promise alone, without adding an unstated restriction.
items.taskText: 'If you complete the pilot, we will reimburse the travel costs.' Nothing is said about other reimbursement arrangements.
options: Anyone who does not complete the pilot is ineligible for any reimbursement.
Anyone reimbursed must have completed the pilot.
The pilot is complete because reimbursement has been promised.
Completing the pilot is sufficient to trigger the promised reimbursement.
items.answer: Completing the pilot is sufficient to trigger the promised reimbursement.
items.explanation: The promise guarantees reimbursement when the stated condition is met.

rationales.Completing the pilot is sufficient to tr: The promise guarantees reimbursement when the stated condition is met.
rationales.Anyone who does not complete the pilot i: The sentence does not say only if; other reimbursement routes remain unstated.
rationales.Anyone reimbursed must have completed th: This reverses the implication and wrongly makes completion necessary for any reimbursement.
rationales.The pilot is complete because reimbursem: A conditional promise does not assert that its condition has already been fulfilled.

findings: Session item repeated begun selection under the same inverted frame.
audit.microSkill: Resisting conditional perfection in a promise
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids silently turning if into if and only if.
